newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish PM needs talks before decision on minister.
newsitem.headline: Polish PM needs talks before decision on minister.

text.p: Poland's prime minister will decide whether to dismiss farm minister Roman Jagielinski after talks, probably next week, with Peasant Party (PSL) chiefs who want him sacked, the PSL leader said on Thursday.
The executive of the PSL, the ruling coalition's smaller party, on Wednesday withdrew support for Jagielinski who is considered among the most liberal Peasant politicians.
The body alleged Jagielinski's farm policies were wrong and proposed that a little-known PSL parliamentary deputy, Jacek Kalinowski, take his posts as deputy prime minister and agriculture minister.
The Peasant party's president Waldemar Pawlak told PAP news agency he had submitted to Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz an official request to fire Jagielinski.
Pawlak was quoted as saying that the prime minister told him he would take no decision on the dismissal before meeting the Peasants' leadership, possibly early next week.
Under the coalition agreement between PSL and the larger, ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD), the Peasants recommend candidates to head the agriculture ministry. @

But a final decision on the appointment now rests with the SLD's Cimoszewicz and with President Aleksander Kwasniewski, unless the Peasants try to oust Jagielinski through a complicated parliamentary procedure.

Jagielinski, who has been exposed in his own party since he unsuccessfully challenged Pawlak for its leadership last year, said he would not resign on his own and left the decision up to the prime minister.
